Energy & Sustainability Manager– Global Workplace & Infrastructure (GWI)

Location – Santa Clara Campus

Company

Applied Materials is the leader in materials engineering solutions used to produce virtually every new chip and advanced display in the world. Our expertise in modifying materials at atomic levels and on an industrial scale helps customers transform possibilities into reality. Our innovations Make Possible® a Better Future. If you’re looking for the next step in your future, consider Applied Materials.

Role

The Energy & Sustainability Manager is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing sustainability initiatives, energy management strategies, and carbon‑reduction programs across the facilities portfolio. This role leads efforts to optimize building performance, reduce consumption, maintain regulatory compliance, and support corporate ESG objectives.

In addition to leading sustainability programs, this position also oversees several key mechanical and life‑safety systems, including EV charger infrastructure, mechanical preventive maintenance, and Fire Life Safety Systems (FLSS), as described in the attached job duties. 

Key Responsibilities

1. Energy Management & Sustainability Leadership

· Develop and implement enterprise‑wide energy and sustainability strategies aligned with corporate carbon‑reduction goals.

· Identify energy‑saving opportunities and lead implementation for HVAC, mechanical systems, lighting, controls, and other major loads.

· Track, analyze, and report energy consumption, utility costs, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, water usage, and waste diversion metrics.

· Lead continuous improvement initiatives to reduce energy intensity and improve operational efficiency.

· Drive sustainability certifications (e.g., LEED, ENERGY STAR, TRUE Zero Waste) where applicable.

· Partner with internal Workplace Manager(s) on cross‑functional sustainability projects and initiatives. 

· 

2. Mechanical Systems Oversight & Preventive Maintenance

· Lead preventive maintenance programs for all major mechanical systems and ensure execution of 100% PM compliance goals. 

· Act as the technical advisor for mechanical system optimization, reliability improvements, and lifecycle planning. 

· Oversee vendor performance for mechanical systems, ensure adherence to SOPs, monitor repairs, and ensure system uptime.

· Support planning, budgeting, and prioritization of mechanical upgrades tied to sustainability goals, efficiency improvements, or compliance drivers.

3. EV Charging Infrastructure Management

· Oversee operation, maintenance, and performance of all EV chargers across the portfolio.

· Ensure EV charging systems maintain 95% uptime and meet 100% safety compliance, as required. 

· Partner with vendors to optimize load management, charging efficiency, demand response, and reporting tools.

· Support expansion planning, infrastructure upgrades, and usage reporting for workplace charging programs. 

4. Fire Life Safety Systems (FLSS)

· Manage the maintenance, testing, and compliance of Fire Life Safety Systems (FLSS).

· Ensure all FLSS meet 100% compliance with regulatory standards and remain fully operational. 

· Coordinate inspections, repairs, documentation, and system upgrades between vendors and internal teams.

5. Compliance & Regulatory Management

· Ensure compliance with local, state, and federal environmental and energy standards.

· Maintain compliance for mechanical systems and fire life safety systems per regulatory requirements. 

· Support sustainability compliance reporting such as CARB, Title 24 benchmarking, waste reporting, or ESG disclosures.

6. Financial Responsibilities

· Identify, scope, and prioritize energy‑efficiency projects with ROI and lifecycle cost justification.

· Manage budgets related to energy programs, mechanical maintenance, and sustainability projects.

· Track utility rebates, grants, and incentives for energy and water efficiency projects.

7. Communication, Training & Stakeholder Engagement

· Develop sustainability communications, building occupant engagement programs, and awareness campaigns.

· Train internal teams and technicians on new sustainability programs, mechanical systems, or operational best practices. 

· Provide dashboards, metrics, and presentations to leadership regarding energy performance and sustainability progress.

Goals & KPIs 

· Achieve 10% annual reduction in energy consumption for assigned systems and initiatives. 

· Maintain 100% preventive maintenance completion for mechanical systems. 

· Maintain 95% EV charger uptime and 100% safety compliance. 

· Ensure 100% compliance for Fire Life Safety Systems. 

Skills & Qualifications

Required Skills

· Strong knowledge of sustainability best practices, energy management, carbon reporting, renewable energy, and building performance optimization.

· Technical understanding of mechanical systems (HVAC, boilers, chillers, pumps, etc.) and preventive maintenance programs.

· Familiarity with fire life safety systems, testing requirements, and compliance frameworks.

· Experience analyzing utility data and using energy management platforms (e.g., EnergyCAP, Lucid, Urjanet, PowerBI).

· Ability to manage vendors, contractors, and cross‑functional project teams.

· Strong analytical, reporting, and communication skills.

Preferred Skills

· Experience with EV charging infrastructure and load management tools. 

· Knowledge of sustainability frameworks such as LEED, WELL, ISO 50001, ENERGY STAR.

· Familiarity with CMMS, BMS, SCADA, and other building management or maintenance systems.

Education & Certifications

· Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Environmental Science, Sustainability, or related field.

· Professional certifications preferred: CEM (Certified Energy Manager), LEED AP, ENV-SP, or equivalent.

Role Summary

The Strategic Sourcing Manager – Facilities & Opex (APAC) is an individual contributor role responsible for executing and operationalizing the Corporate Global Workplace Infrastructure (GWI) Category Strategy for General Facilities and Operating Expenses (Opex) across the APAC region. The role focuses on strengthening site-level coverage, driving consistency and standardization, and improving transparency and resiliency across critical facilities services.

This position partners closely with regional site teams and corporate stakeholders to ensure disciplined sourcing execution, effective supplier management, and robust governance aligned to global playbooks, while remaining responsive to local operational needs.

General Duties

• Execute sourcing and supplier management activities for General Facilities and Facilities-related Opex categories across APAC in alignment with corporate procurement and GWI strategies.

• Provide day-to-day sourcing, contracting, and commercial support to site and regional facilities teams.

• Act as a subject matter expert (SME) for facilities services sourcing, supporting consistent execution across multiple countries and sites.

• Maintain sourcing documentation, contracts, pricing records, and audit-ready files in accordance with corporate governance standards.

Category Strategy Execution (Facilities & Opex)

• Execute the Corporate GWI Category Strategy for General Facilities and Opex services across APAC.

• Translate global category strategies, standards, and playbooks into practical regional and site-level execution.

• Support multi-year category roadmaps covering facilities management, soft services, hard services, utilities-related Opex, and other critical site services.

• Identify regional market dynamics, cost drivers, and risks impacting facilities Opex performance.

Site Coverage & SME Support

• Strengthen site-level sourcing and supplier management coverage across APAC facilities portfolios.

• Provide hands-on SME support to site facilities teams on sourcing strategy, supplier selection, commercial terms, and performance management.

• Enable consistent application of sourcing processes, tools, templates, and governance across all supported sites.

• Support onboarding and capability uplift of regional and site stakeholders on global sourcing standards and expectations.

Supplier Management, Contracts & Performance

• Standardize supplier management approaches, contracts, SLAs, and KPIs across facilities and Opex categories using the global GWI playbook.

• Support development and maintenance of regional and site-level master service agreements, rate cards, and service catalogs.

• Maintain supplier scorecards, monitor KPIs, and track performance trends across cost, service quality, safety, and compliance.

• Drive corrective action plans and performance improvement initiatives with suppliers in collaboration with site teams.

Resiliency & Risk Management

• Drive resiliency strategies for critical facilities services, including dual-sourcing and contingency planning.

• Identify single-source risks, capacity constraints, and supplier dependencies across the APAC region.

• Partner with regional stakeholders to develop mitigation plans for supply continuity, service reliability, and operational risk.

Spend Visibility & Analytics

• Improve visibility into facilities and Opex spend across APAC through structured reporting and analytics.

• Analyze Opex cost drivers, supplier pricing structures, and consumption patterns.

• Develop dashboards and reports to track spend, savings, performance, and risk for category leaders and stakeholders.

• Partner with Finance to support budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis related to facilities Opex.

Governance, Compliance & Standardization

• Ensure compliance with corporate procurement policies, internal controls, and commercial governance requirements.

• Enforce consistent use of approved suppliers, contracts, SLAs, and KPIs across sites.

• Support harmonization of facilities sourcing and supplier management under a unified regional operating model.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Partner closely with Facilities, GWI, Site Operations, EH&S, Finance, Legal, and regional leadership teams.

• Act as the primary sourcing interface for facilities-related Opex topics in APAC.

• Represent sourcing in regional reviews, operational meetings, and governance forums.

Required Qualifications

• 7+ years of sourcing, procurement, or category management experience, preferably within facilities management, services sourcing, or Opex-driven categories.

• Strong experience in supplier management, contract negotiation, SLA/KPI development, and performance management.

• Demonstrated ability to execute global category strategies within a regional or multi-country environment.

• Strong analytical skills with experience in spend analysis, cost modeling, and performance reporting.

• Ability to manage multiple stakeholders across geographies and balance global standards with local requirements.

• Strong communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills.

Generate internal documentation for products, presentations, and technical reports

As a Field Service Engineer [Customer Engineer] at Applied Materials, you serve as the direct liaison with customers, collaborating closely to install, maintain, and upgrade equipment. You'll use digital analytics for troubleshooting and apply basic diagnostic techniques to assess and address technical issues. Your responsibilities include performing preventative and corrective maintenance on various systems such as electrical, vacuum, mechanical, plasma, hydraulic, and gas systems. Additionally, you'll coordinate and communicate directly with customers to ensure smooth operations and exceptional service.
 

 

Role Responsibilities: 

Install, maintain, and upgrade customer equipment

Apply troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, as well as company diagnostic tools and documentation, to solve complex equipment issues

Follow and generate documented procedures and published task plans

Communicate with customers and internal business units, lead projects as necessary

Train and mentor junior Field Service Engineers [Customer Engineers]

Fulfill additional duties, as assigned

Minimum Qualifications: 

Completion of an Associate degree or comparable military technical training and field service experience

7-10 years of work experience in semiconductor industry or other equipment support industry

Advanced mechanical aptitude with pneumatics, hydraulics, electronics, vacuum, and/or thermodynamics

Strong knowledge of hand tools and their appropriate usage, including digital multimeters

Advanced knowledge of wafer processing parameters

Effective written and verbal communication skills

Basic knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint 

Possession of a valid driver’s license and the ability to obtain a passport, if travel is required. 

Able to meet all on-site requirements, including safety, environmental guidelines, and COVID-19 protocols

Bachelor’s Degree

Project management skills and ability to lead key customer and internal product meetings

This position often requires extensive walking, standing for extended periods of time, working in tight spaces, bending, squatting, twisting, kneeling, reaching, climbing stairs and ladders, working at height, lifting up to 35 lbs., the ability to distinguish between colors and working with electricity, the ability to work in an environment with noise that may be difficult for some individuals with sensitivity to noise, and the use of hand and power tools. Additionally, because this position generally involves working in a clean room, it requires the use of appropriate Personal Protective Equipment such as coveralls, hoods, booties, safety glasses, gloves, respirators, chemical aprons, and face shields.

As a Field Service Engineer [Customer Engineer] at Applied Materials, you serve as the direct liaison with customers, collaborating closely to install, maintain, and upgrade equipment. You'll use digital analytics for troubleshooting and apply basic diagnostic techniques to assess and address technical issues. Your responsibilities include performing preventative and corrective maintenance on various systems such as electrical, vacuum, mechanical, plasma, hydraulic, and gas systems. Additionally, you'll coordinate and communicate directly with customers to ensure smooth operations and exceptional service.
 

 

Key Responsibilities

Daily Management: ​

In addition to CE responsibilities, shift Leads primary focus is to help Ops Lead allocate the shift resources to best meet the customers expectation while mentoring, providing assistance, and training to junior CEs and PMTs ​

Be proactive, looking ahead at upcoming maintenance and prepare parts/resources. ​

Communicate and manage customers (PMs and CMs) priorities, needs, and expectations through Ops Lead.​ ​

Review AMAT KPIs daily and drive improvements for failing CAP groups with poor availability ​ ​

Ensure no staffing is working on their own if not qualified ​

Ensure all new hires/contractors/loan labor review sites expectations and protocols (safety, qualification, TRTs, and WSS) ​ ​

Help Ops Leads enforce and complete the priorities of the day by checking in on CEs, PMTs ​

Assist in all areas of the fab and cover areas that are short resources​ ​

Communicate escalations, extended downs and all matters of unsatisfactory issues to Ops Leads​ ​

Assist with escalations/communications on all prolonged/chronic downs to CIP Engineer and Operations Lead. ​

Also assist with open actions plans and ensure they are up-to-date so the on coming shift is prepared to resume where left off ​ ​

Mentor/Motivate/Develop CEs, PMTs ​

Instill in CEs methodologies in daily work activities, i.e. troubleshooting, procedure writing and identifying areas of improvement throughout the site​ ​

Provide Shift Personnel (CE’s, PMT’s) feedback to Ops Lead for Quarterly Reviews and for issues that arise thru the shift related to personnel issues​ ​

Attend any required customer facing meetings as a representative of Applied Materials. ​

Teams Meetings & Chats: ​

Act as the point of contact for morning and end of day meetings with customers when giving updates on equipment statuses. ​

Follow up with CE’s to ensure they meet the expectation of updating the team chat, passdown and site specific MES (manufacturing execution system) ​

Present the morning stand down. ​

 TKM & Parts: ​

Review parts are confirmed and returned within when received, removed, installed real time. Follow up with team members and remove any bottlenecks hindering part returns. Escalate if Team member isn’t being compliant. ​

Review daily TKM and ensure availability of required kits for upcoming PM’s. ​

Safety: ​

Conduct a Weekly SWA (Safety Walk-Around), and coach CE’s to conduct weekly SWA’s. ​

Other Requirements: This is a physically demanding position that often requires extensive walking, standing for extended periods of time, working in tight spaces, bending, squatting, twisting, kneeling, reaching, climbing stairs and ladders, lifting up to 35 lbs., the ability to distinguish between colors, the ability to work in an environment with noise that may be difficult for some individuals with sensitivity to noise, and the use of hand and power tools. Additionally, because this position generally involves working in a clean room, it requires the use of appropriate Personal Protective Equipment such as coveralls, hoods, booties, safety glasses, gloves, respirators, chemical aprons, and face shields.

Job Description: Senior Technical Team Leader – Calibration Systems 

We are looking for an experienced Senior Technical Team Leader to lead the development of calibration systems software for advanced electron microscope columns. 

What’s in it for you? 

You will lead a small, highly skilled team while remaining hands-on in architecture, design, and implementation. This role combines scientific computing, image processing, and distributed systems to enable fully automated calibration workflows used in semiconductor manufacturing and materials science. You will work at the intersection of software engineering, physics, and real laboratory hardware, building systems with real-world impact and stringent performance requirements. 

Our Group 

We are part of the R&D department of a major brand new and exciting Product, responsible for developing the next generation software and algorithm solutions that will power Applied Materials’ cutting-edge metrology and inspection system. 

What you'll be doing 

Technical Leadership 

• Lead architectural design and technical decision making for the Column Calibration System 

• Establish and enforce coding standards and design patterns (Repository, Service Layer, Dependency Injection) 

• Conduct code reviews with a strong focus on type safety, testability, performance, and scientific correctness 

• Mentor 2–4 developers in Python best practices, scientific computing, and distributed systems 

• Drive adoption and continuous improvement of AI-assisted development workflows 

• Own technology stack evolution decisions and third-party library selection 

Hands-On Development 

• Architect and implement complex, stateful calibration workflows 

• Design and build microservice-style solutions using REST and gRPC APIs 

• Develop scientific computing modules using NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, and Matplotlib 

• Implement robust numerical algorithms with fitting, retry, and fallback logic 

• Optimize performance-critical image processing paths for real-time focus score calculation 

• Build interactive web-based monitoring and visualization tools using Dash and Plotly 

• Develop hardware simulation modes to support algorithm development and automated testing 

• Write comprehensive unit and integration tests 

Project Collaboration 

• Break down epics into clear, implementable stories with well-defined acceptance criteria 

• Work closely with physicists and microscope operators to validate and refine calibration algorithms 

• Participate in sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives 

• Document architectural decisions, APIs, and system designs 

• Collaborate with DevOps on CI/CD pipelines, deployment, and system monitoring 

What you should have 

Experience 

• 8+ years of professional software development experience 

• 3+ years in a technical lead or senior developer role 

• 2+ years working on scientific computing or data-intensive systems 

Technical Skills 

• Expert-level Python, including type hints, async/await, and modern idioms 

• Experience with FastAPI or similar Python web frameworks 

• Strong background in NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, and Matplotlib 

• Experience with Pydantic for data validation and serialization 

• RESTful API design and OpenAPI/Swagger 

• Microservices architecture and distributed systems 

• Solid understanding of software design patterns (Repository, Service Layer, Dependency Injection) 

Software Engineering Practices 

• Unit and integration testing (pytest, unittest) 

• Static type checking (mypy, Pylance) 

• Git-based workflows and code reviews 

• CI/CD pipelines and automated testing 

• Docker and containerized deployments 

• Linux-based development environments 

Scientific & Domain Knowledge 

• Numerical algorithms and optimization techniques 

• Image processing fundamentals 

• Familiarity with hardware control or instrumentation software 

Leadership & Communication 

• Proven experience mentoring and developing engineers 

• Strong technical documentation and writing skills

• Ability to clearly communicate complex technical concepts to diverse audiences 

Education 

• B.Sc. in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field or equivalent industry experience with demonstrated expertise in scientific computing 

Preferred background areas include computational physics, applied mathematics, image processing, optics, microscopy, signal processing, or numerical analysis. 

Nice to have 

• Experience with Dash or Plotly 

• Familiarity with electron microscopy or semiconductor manufacturing equipment 

• Performance profiling and optimization 

• Async HTTP clients (httpx, aiohttp) 

• Experience with C/C++ or Java backend development 

• Linux system administration 

• Agile/Scrum development experience 

Technology Stack 

• Python 3.9+ 

• FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn 

• NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Pillow 

• Dash, Plotly 

• pytest, mypy, Docker, Git 

• MinIO, Redis, JSON-based storage 

• Linux (Ubuntu)

As a Field Service Engineer [Customer Engineer] at Applied Materials, you serve as the direct liaison with customers, collaborating closely to install, maintain, and upgrade equipment. Collaborate with Senior Field Service Engineers [Customer Engineers] in installing, maintaining, and upgrading customer equipment

Fulfill additional duties, as assigned

As a Manufacturing Technician, you'll work hands-on in a cleanroom environment to build and test our multimillion-dollar display and wafer fabrication equipment that’s behind the technology we use every day. You'll be responsible for building, repairing, and testing various types of equipment--including electrical, electro-mechanical, vacuum, and pneumatic assemblies, subassemblies, and components. You will perform electro-mechanical assembly operations, troubleshooting, and repairs-- and perform audits to ensure necessary parts are available and inspected for defects. Utilizes routine work orders, schematics, wiring diagrams, parts and wire lists, written and/or verbal instructions to build, repair and/or test electrical, electro-mechanical, vacuum, pneumatic assemblies, subassemblies and components.

Role Summary

The Global Category Manager - Human Capital Services is the strategic owner of an assigned category of spend, accountable for defining the global category strategy and delivering outcomes across value capture, stakeholder experience, and risk management. This role sets direction (the “WHAT”) through category strategies, supplier portfolio and segmentation decisions, governance, and demand/value roadmaps, while enabling scaled execution (the “HOW”) through Strategic Sourcing Managers and the Sourcing Center of Excellence (SCoE). Operating in a center‑led ‘one house’ model, the Global Category Manager orchestrates cross‑functional alignment, ensures consistent global standards with regional nuance, and drives measurable business impact for Applied Materials.

Role at a Glance

Job Title

Global Category Manager - Human Capital Services

Organization

Global Sourcing & Procurement (GSP) – Global Category & Sourcing

Reports To

Category Leader / Portfolio Leader (per org design)

Primary Purpose

Own the category strategy, supplier portfolio, governance, and outcome delivery across the enterprise.

Primary Interfaces

Business Unit leaders/stakeholders, Strategic Sourcing Managers, SCoE Leaders, Supplier Executives, Finance (Value Capture), Risk/TPRM, Contracting CoE/Legal, Operations/BPO

Operating Model

Category defines strategy and guardrails; Sourcing executes and refines through data/insights; one unified global team.

Scope Anchors

Global category strategy + wave plan; supplier segmentation and SRM; demand management; risk and compliance integration; category councils and performance governance.

Category Scope
Talent Acquisition (TA) Services

Own global category strategy, sourcing, and supplier governance for recruiting, executive search, and assessment services, aligned to enterprise hiring demand.

Lead supplier segmentation, commercial models, and performance management (SLAs/KPIs), partnering with HR while Procurement retains ownership of supplier selection and contracts.

Talent Retention (TR) Services

Define and execute category strategies for benefits administration, global mobility, immigration, relocation, and expatriate services.

Drive market intelligence, sourcing decisions, contracting frameworks, and supplier performance governance in support of HR‑led programs.

Learning & Development (L&D) Services

Lead category strategy and supplier management for learning content, platforms, leadership development, and coaching services.

Optimize supplier portfolios and commercial outcomes while partnering with HR on demand alignment and capability priorities.

Mission Alignment (GSP “Definition of Winning”)

Value Capture: establish multi‑year value levers (savings, cost avoidance, productivity, revenue enablement) and deliver results through a governed pipeline.

Client Journey: build proactive stakeholder engagement models and predictable delivery experiences through clear intake, governance, and communication.

Risk Management: embed third‑party and supply‑market risk thinking into category strategies, supplier decisions, and contracting guardrails.

Optimize Capability: enable the organization through playbooks, standards, and a talent pipeline that improves execution quality over time.

Key Responsibilities

1) Global Category Strategy & Roadmap Ownership

Define and maintain a multi‑year global category strategy that aligns to Applied and GSP priorities, including clear goals, value levers, and execution waves.

Establish category scope, taxonomy alignment, and a demand/supply perspective (demand signals, business requirements, supply market dynamics).

Develop and refresh a category roadmap that sequences initiatives by impact, urgency, risk, and capacity, maintaining a forward‑looking pipeline.

2) Supplier Portfolio Strategy, Segmentation & SRM

Own supplier portfolio design and segmentation (strategic, preferred, transactional) and define the engagement model for each segment.

Lead strategic supplier relationship management (SRM) for priority suppliers: performance, innovation, commercial governance, and executive alignment.

Drive supplier rationalization and consolidation opportunities that improve leverage, simplify operations, and reduce total cost of ownership.

3) Business Partnership (BRM) & Stakeholder Governance

Serve as a trusted advisor to business unit leadership; translate business objectives into category strategies and sourcing priorities.

Lead category councils and governance forums (e.g., value/risk reviews, supplier performance reviews) to drive decisions, alignment, and accountability.

Set stakeholder engagement rhythms and communication standards so the category experience is consistent across regions and teams.

4) Value Capture, Financial Stewardship & Performance Management

Define and govern the category value pipeline (initiatives, baselines, assumptions, milestones) and partner with Finance for validation and reporting.

Establish outcome metrics beyond savings (service levels, speed/cycle time, quality, compliance, risk reduction, innovation) and monitor performance.

Ensure sourcing and contracting approaches are aligned to approved category strategies and buying channel guidance.

5) Risk, Resilience & Compliance Integration

Integrate supplier risk considerations into category plans, including third‑party risk management (TPRM) triggers and mitigation actions.

Partner with Risk/TPRM, Legal, Privacy/Data Governance, and Compliance teams to ensure category decisions and supplier selections protect Applied.

Proactively monitor supply market risks and translate signals into actions (dual sourcing, contract protections, contingency plans).

6) Execution Orchestration Through Sourcing (One House Model)

Translate strategy into sourcing wave plans and clearly defined playbooks/guardrails for Strategic Sourcing Managers and SCoE execution teams.

Oversee implementation progress and remove barriers; ensure handoffs and workflow between Category and Sourcing are efficient and predictable.

Continuously refine strategy based on execution learnings, market feedback, and data insights (strategy ↔ execution feedback loop).

7) Capability Building & Change Leadership

Champion standard ways of working, templates, and governance that reduce variability and improve speed and quality across the category.

Support the talent pipeline by coaching and developing Strategic Sourcing Managers and SCoE practitioners; enable role clarity and development paths.

Lead change initiatives within the category (process, tools, supplier operating models) and drive adoption through clear messaging and reinforcement.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, Finance, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

Demonstrated category management leadership: building and executing category strategies, supplier segmentation, and governance models.

Strong commercial expertise: negotiations, contract strategy, and total cost/value analysis in complex, multi‑stakeholder environments.

Proven ability to lead in a global, matrixed organization—driving alignment across regions, functions, and senior stakeholders.

Experience integrating risk and compliance considerations into supplier and category decisions.

Preferred

Experience in semiconductor or high‑tech indirect categories (e.g., IT, facilities, technical services, labor/services) and global supplier ecosystems.

Experience with structured category strategy programs, analytics-enabled decision making, and formal value capture governance.

Professional certifications (e.g., CPSM, CIPS, CPM) and/or MBA/MS in a relevant discipline.

Experience leading transformations (process standardization, operating model change, digital procurement tools) and scaling best practices.

Core Competencies (What “Great” Looks Like)

Strategic thinking & roadmap design: turns business needs and market dynamics into a clear category plan and sequence of work.

Business partnership: earns trust with executives; frames decisions, trade‑offs, and value in business language.

Supplier leadership: drives SRM rigor, performance, and supplier-led innovation; manages escalations effectively.

Analytical leadership: uses data to prioritize, challenge assumptions, and quantify both cost and non-cost value.

Governance discipline: establishes predictable cadences, decision forums, and accountability mechanisms.

Change leadership: drives adoption of new ways of working and reinforces clarity of roles and handoffs.

Success Measures

Category outcomes: delivered and validated value aligned to targets (savings, cost avoidance, productivity, and/or risk reduction).

Pipeline health: forward-looking, prioritized pipeline with clear owners, milestones, and predictable execution cadence.

Supplier performance: improved supplier AQSCIR outcomes (assurance, quality, service, cost, innovation, relationship) and reduced critical risk exposure.

Stakeholder experience: improved satisfaction and reduced friction through clear governance, communication, and faster cycle times.

Operating model effectiveness: consistent strategy-to-execution flow and reduced rework/hand-off delays across Category, Sourcing, Contracting, and Ops.

Planner IV is a senior-level contributor leading complex planning activities across product life cycles and scaling product performance through systems, data, and cross-functional influence. Responsibilities include planning, forecasting, analyzing, and evaluating service parts requirements to ensure delivery of right quantities to the right locations on time. The role requires advanced analytical abilities, critical thinking, effective communication, and proven leadership to address product planning complexities and achieve successful results.

The ideal candidate has deep demand planning expertise, operates effectively amid ambiguity, possesses strategic vision, and translates business and customer needs into actionable plans. This position shapes planning deliverables, influences cross-functional teams, and drives initiatives to enhance service performance, scalability, and operational efficiency.

Roles & Responsibilities:

End-to-End Parts Planning: Oversee all aspects of demand forecasting, inventory management, ramp planning, and transition planning for designated products. Own planning deliverables throughout each stage of the product lifecycle, including new product introduction (NPI), transitions, ramp, and end-of-life processes.

Strategic Planning and Development: Design and implement planning methodologies that reflect overall business goals and service targets. Enhance planning workflows, tools, data models, and visualizations to enable scalable operations. Convert organizational needs into clear, actionable planning tactics.

Collaboration and Communication: Partner closely with other Operations teams, Service Business Units (SBUs), Business Units (BUs) and Engineering to synchronize planning activities with business priorities. Influence outcomes without formal authority by using data-driven insights, effective communication that frames tradeoffs and aligning incentives.

Risk Management & Decision Support: Identify and evaluate potential risks in supply, demand, cost, and service performance. Analyze tradeoffs involving availability, cost, and inventory investment to guide decisions. Manage exceptions while delivering clear recommendations to leadership.

Project Management: Lead funded projects to completion on schedule and within budget, while offering technical guidance to team members.

Performance Tracking and Improvement: Track product performance, identify improvement opportunities through detailed data analysis, and implement corrective measures to boost efficiency and effectiveness in planning operations.

Leadership and Development: Offer informal guidance and mentorship to junior planners, encourage adherence to best practices, and nurture a culture focused on continuous improvement and productivity gains.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university in Supply Chain, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations, or Business is required; an MBA is considered an asset.

At least 8 years of experience with a minimum of 6 years’ experience in inventory management, supply planning, material planning, or demand planning, including KPI definition, measurement, and control.

Background in the semiconductor industry is a must, with experience in Service Parts, Warranty, or Service Planning experience preferred.

Exceptional analytical abilities, with a proven track record of developing data-driven solutions and alternatives. Proficiency in data analytics tools such as Tableau, Power BI, SQL is highly desirable. Skilled in interpreting complex data sets to identify trends and issues.

Excellent communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with team members, internal stakeholders, and customers.

Demonstrated problem-solving, critical thinking, and attention to detail.

Extensive functional knowledge of ERP and supply chain planning systems (e.g., SAP, SPP, Oracle).

Proven leadership capabilities in managing complex planning projects and initiatives.

Strong business acumen, with a comprehensive understanding of Applied Materials’ key business drivers.

Ability to frame ambiguous planning problems and recommend paths forward and drive results through sound judgment and influence.

Focus on developing mechanisms, systems and processes, not workarounds

Job Summary:​

The Graphite Purification, DIW Sonication, and CVD Process Operator is responsible for preparing and processing graphite components through deionized water (DIW) sonication, high-temperature purification, and Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) coating. This role ensures strict adherence to standard operating procedures (SOPs), safety protocols, and quality requirements for producing high-purity, coated graphite parts used in semiconductor applications.

Key Responsibilities:

Graphite Purification Process:

Load & unload graphite components into high-temperature purification furnaces

Monitor furnace parameters (temperature, time, gas flow) during purification cycles

Perform system purging and cooling steps according to recipes

Ensure minimal contamination and proper handling of ultra-pure materials

DIW Sonication Cleaning

Prepare graphite parts for DIW ultrasonic cleaning (pre-rinse, degrease, etc.)

Operate ultrasonic baths with controlled time, temperature, and frequency

Inspect parts post-sonication for residual contamination

Maintain cleanliness of DIW system and filter integrity

CVD Coating Process

Load graphite parts onto fixtures and into CVD reactor chambers

Monitor recipe-driven CVD cycles (temperature, pressure, precursor gases)

Ensure coating uniformity, thickness, and adhesion through basic inspection

Perform post-process chamber cleaning and maintenance

Quality Control & Inspection

Conduct visual inspection for cracks, warpage, coating defects, or contamination

Use basic metrology tools to confirm dimensions or part condition post-process

Prepare parts for QA team verification

Documentation & Reporting

Accurately record batch information, process conditions, and lot traceability

Complete run sheets, checklists, and quality logs

Escalate process deviations or equipment abnormalities to engineers or leads

Equipment Care & Safety

Follow all safety protocols (EHS, chemical, gas handling, PPE)

Maintain cleanliness of process tools, chambers, and work environment

Perform minor tool maintenance or assist with PMs under supervision

Support continuous improvement initiatives and SOP updates

Qualifications

HS diploma or equivalent; technical training preferred

1-3 years of experience in semiconductor, graphite, or coating process operations

Basic knowledge of high-temperature furnaces, vacuum systems, and gas controls

Familiarity with deionized water cleaning and ultrasonic systems

Attention to detail and ability to follow strict SOPs and documentation practices

Comfortable working in a cleanroom or controlled environments

Team player with strong work ethic & willingness to learn complex processes

Other Requirements: This is a very physically demanding position that often requires standing for extended periods of time, walking, bending, squatting, twisting, kneeling, reaching, lifting, the ability to distinguish between colors, the ability to work in an environment with noise that may be difficult for some individuals with sensitivity to noise, the use of hand and power tools, and driving or operating heavy machinery including forklifts.

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Process Integration Engineer to join our Photonics Platform Business Group. In this role, you will enable the transition of advanced optical device technologies from R&D into scalable manufacturing. You will work closely with cross-functional engineering teams to define, develop, and optimize process flows for cutting-edge semiconductor and photonics devices.

Key Responsibilities:

Drive end-to-end process integration for advanced semiconductor device fabrication.

Define and optimize process flows to achieve performance, yield, and reliability targets.

Collaborate with module owners (lithography, etch, deposition, metrology, etc.) to align process development with integration requirements.

Conduct design-of-experiments (DOE) to identify process sensitivities and improve manufacturability.

Analyze optical test data to provide feedback for process tuning and device improvement.

Collaborate with design, process, and operations teams to ensure smooth technology transfer into volume manufacturing.

Troubleshoot integration issues and drive root-cause analysis for process-related failures.

Support technology roadmaps by contributing to process integration strategy and scalability.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define and implement process integration methodologies and continuous improvement initiatives.

Stay updated with the latest advancements and industry trends in process integration to drive innovation.

Provide technical guidance and support to junior engineers and technicians, fostering a collaborative and knowledge-sharing work environment.

Degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field. PhD or Masters preferred.

Work experience of at least 5 years. Proven experience (>3 years) in process integration, preferably R&D within a high-volume manufacturing environment.

Strong understanding of nanotechnology processes, including lithography, etch, deposition, and metrology.

Proficient in statistical data analysis and process optimization and control techniques (e.g., Design of Experiments, SPC, JMP).

Ability to read and understand layout files (industry-standard such as GDS and OASIS) and familiarity optical proximity correction (OPC) methodologies is a plus.

Knowledge of optics principles and photonic components and systems is desirable.

Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.

Knowledge of industry standards and best practices in semiconductor manufacturing, such as ISO, SEMI, and ITAR regulations, and Project management skills are a plus.

We are looking for a Product/Program Manager to join the SW GenAI Core Team, which is driving a transformative corporate initiative to achieve significant productivity improvement through AI adoption, starting with our software organization and expanding across the entire R&D landscape. The role involves validating implementation of AI productivity playbooks across product groups, tracking adoption metrics, gathering stakeholder feedback, and connecting insights to surface opportunities and gaps in our GenAI transformation journey.

What's in it for you?

This is an opportunity to be at the heart of Applied Materials' AI transformation, impacting the entire R&D organization while working with cutting-edge GenAI tools and methodologies. You'll gain exposure to multiple business units, collaborate with diverse stakeholders across the organization, and play a critical role in shaping how we adopt and measure AI-driven productivity improvements. Your insights and execution will directly contribute to ambitious organizational goals and drive real impact.

Our Group:

The SW GenAI Core Team is a newly established team (~5 people) leading Applied Materials' corporate-wide AI-Driven Productivity Program. We develop methodologies, frameworks, AI tools, best practices (BKMs), and playbooks while defining adoption plans and measurement tools to achieve ambitious productivity improvement targets by end of 2026. We operate in a dynamic, matrix-management environment collaborating across PDC R&D centers in Israel and Bangalore, working closely with Applied Materials HQ AI leadership to align on strategy and best practices.

What you'll be doing:

Validate Implementation Across Groups: Track and validate the adoption of productivity playbooks across multiple software product groups, ensuring implementations meet defined acceptance criteria and organizational standards.

Discovery & Gap Analysis: Create and maintain productivity heat maps per product, identify gaps between current practices and productivity goals, and surface insights that indicate missing capabilities or process improvements needed.

Voice of Customer: Act as the bridge between field teams and the SW GenAI Core Team by gathering feedback from software managers, team leads, and product stakeholders, synthesizing patterns, and escalating issues to leadership.

Data-Driven Monitoring: Track adoption of metrics through dashboards and scorecards, monitor products against acceptance criteria, and provide regular status updates on playbook adoption and productivity improvements.

Stakeholder Collaboration: Work closely with software managers, team leaders, product managers, and system engineers across multiple groups to facilitate adoption, organize hackathons and adoption events, and ensure alignment on productivity goals.

Connect the Dots: Synthesize disparate feedback from various stakeholders to identify systemic issues, surface opportunities for new playbooks or tools, and contribute to the strategic direction of the productivity program.

Make Things Happen: Drive execution with a bias for action. We believe in delivery over endless planning - you'll be expected to take ownership, navigate obstacles, and ensure initiatives move from concept to reality.

What Should You Have?

B.Sc. in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or related field. MBA is an advantage.

3-5 years of professional experience with demonstrated project management skills.

Technical background or ability to understand software development concepts and SDLC

Product mindset - ability to think strategically about solutions, understand user needs, and drive product-oriented outcomes.

Get things done attitude - proven track record of executing initiatives, driving projects to completion, and delivering results with minimal supervision.

Data literacy with hands-on skills - ability to analyze metrics, interpret dashboards, derive actionable insights from data, AND technically connect to/extract data from ticketing systems, project management tools, and data sources for decision-making.

Stakeholder management - experience collaborating with diverse stakeholders across multiple teams and demonstrated ability to influence without direct authority.

Attention to detail while maintaining the ability to see the big picture - balance tactical execution with strategic thinking.

Connecting the dots - ability to synthesize feedback from multiple sources, identify patterns, and surface actionable insights.

AI mindset with hands-on experience - natural inclination to leverage GenAI tools in daily work, openness to AI-augmented workflows, and proven ability to build small projects or prototypes with AI tools. This role requires rolling up your sleeves and working directly with data and AI systems, not just coordinating meetings.

Fast learner and embrace change - ability to quickly understand technical concepts, adapt to new tools and methodologies, and operate comfortably in a fast-evolving environment where priorities shift, new AI capabilities emerge frequently, and agility is essential.

What Gives You an Advantage?

Analytics or data visualization experience.

Prior experience in semiconductor or technology industry.

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Microsoft 365 (M365) Platform Engineer to join our dynamic team. The ideal candidate will have extensive knowledge across the Microsoft 365 suite and related services (e.g., Teams, Copilot, SharePoint/OneDrive, Office apps, Entra ID, licensing, and security/compliance capabilities), along with a strong background in PowerShell scripting, automation, low-code/no-code solutions.

Role Summary

A Microsoft 365 Platform Engineer is needed to provide technical expertise for enterprise productivity and collaboration services. This role is accountable for administration, strategy, governance, security/compliance alignment, and operational excellence across core Microsoft 365 workloads, including Teams and Copilot. The engineer will support implementations and rollouts, drive feature adoption and change management, build automation and reporting using PowerShell and Microsoft Graph, and act as an escalation point for complex issues. The role also includes maintaining documentation and delivering training to end users and support teams.

Key Responsibilities

Microsoft 365 Platform Ownership & Engineering

Serves as a senior Microsoft 365 engineer, accountable for service health, user experience, and operational maturity across core M365 workloads.

Defines and maintains Microsoft 365 service standards, including governance, lifecycle management, and administrative operating procedures.

Partners with Identity, Security, Compliance, Networking, Endpoint, and the Service Desk teams to ensure Microsoft 365 aligns with enterprise controls and business needs.

Implementations, Rollouts & Change Management

Drives end-to-end delivery of Microsoft 365 initiatives, including pilots, phased rollouts, feature launches, service migrations, and operational enhancements across multiple workloads.

Owns change management activities including release planning, adoption readiness, communications planning, and support enablement.

Tracks Microsoft 365 updates and service changes; evaluates impact, risks, and dependencies; converts findings into actionable implementation plans.

Productivity & Collaboration Capabilities

Administers and optimizes collaboration and content experiences across Microsoft 365, including Teams (meetings, messaging, apps), and other services.

Ensures service configuration supports a consistent, secure, and reliable end-user experience at enterprise scale.

Governance, Security, and Compliance

Implements and administers governance controls across Microsoft 365 including policies, lifecycle management, naming conventions, templates, sharing standards, and standard configurations.

Collaborates with security and compliance stakeholders to support enterprise requirements such as data protection, retention, eDiscovery, auditing, and access controls (including Microsoft Purview capabilities, as applicable).

Automation, APIs, and Reporting

Automates and streamlines reporting and administrative tasks using PowerShell, Power Automate, and Microsoft Graph API.

Enables governance workflows (provisioning, policy application, lifecycle actions) through automation.

Generates operational, adoption, and compliance reporting; reduces manual effort and improves configuration consistency at scale.

Builds metrics and reporting to monitor usage, adoption, and policy compliance.

Troubleshooting, Incident Response & Continuous Improvement

Acts as a senior escalation point for complex M365-related incidents and service degradation; drives root cause analysis and long-term remediation.

Collaborates closely with L2/L3 operations teams to manage support escalations, ensuring timely resolution.

Manages vendor support engagements (e.g., Microsoft support cases), ensuring structured troubleshooting, thorough documentation, and timely resolution.

Produces problem records and post-incident learnings; implements preventive controls and service improvements.

Documentation, Communications, and Training

Writes clear end-user communications (service updates, feature announcements, “what’s changing,” adoption tips).

Produces and maintains technical documentation for support teams (KBs, troubleshooting guides, standard operating procedures).

Delivers training and knowledge transfer for end users and support teams, enabling self-service and faster resolution.

Required Skills & Experience

5+ years of experience administering Microsoft 365 services in a large enterprise environment. This includes hands-on administration expertise across multiple Microsoft 365 workloads such as Entra ID, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online/OneDrive, Teams, and Microsoft 365 Apps.

1+ year of experience administering Microsoft 365 Copilot and/or other generative AI capabilities in an enterprise environment, including configuration and user enablement.

Strong automation and scripting skills using PowerShell (advanced patterns, modular scripts, logging, error handling) and Power Automate.

Well-versed in essential Azure services, including Entra ID, Automation Accounts, and Enterprise Apps.

Comprehensive understanding of Microsoft 365 licensing models and service plans.

Experience working with Microsoft Graph API—including authentication concepts, permissions scopes, app registrations, and REST patterns.

Demonstrated ability to drive enterprise rollouts and implementations, including support readiness and change management.

Strong troubleshooting skills across identity, policy, client behavior, configuration, and service components.

Proven ability to write high-quality documentation and communications for technical and non-technical audiences.

Experience providing training/enablement to end users and support teams.

Qualifications

5+ years in a Microsoft 365 engineering/administration role.

Demonstrated depth in at least one major Microsoft 365 workload (e.g., Teams, Exchange Online, SharePoint/OneDrive, Entra ID) and working knowledge across the broader suite.

Experience operating within structured IT processes and collaborating across technical teams and business stakeholders.

Relevant Microsoft certifications such as MS‑102, MS‑700, SC‑300/SC‑400, or AZ‑104 are a plus, but not required.

Senior Director, Supplier Engineering

BUSINESS UNIT: Varian Semiconductor Equipment (VSE) – Silicon Systems Group (SSG)

LOCATION: Gloucester, MA

ROLE SUMMARY

The Senior Director of Supplier Engineering leads a global, multidisciplinary technical organization responsible for building a resilient, cost‑effective, and innovation‑enabled supply chain. This role shapes and executes long‑range strategies that enhance supply continuity, scale engineering capability, strengthen supplier partnerships across regions, and ensure enterprise alignment. The position drives local and global collaboration, enables cost transformation, improves supplier readiness, and builds the Best Known Methods (BKMs) library deployed across the enterprise.

A critical component of this role is the ability to present strategy to executive leadership, influence direction, and garner cross‑functional buy‑in across Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Finance, and Product organizations. Organization awareness and ability to influence others is crucial for this role.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership & Business Alignment

• Define and execute the multi‑year strategy for Supplier Engineering aligned with BU priorities, product roadmaps, and Applied’s global supply chain objectives.

• Provide clear strategic direction to improve supply continuity, supplier capability, engineering quality, and cost structure. Requires strong cross-functional alignment with goals and objectives of the Varian and GSC AOP’s to enable corporate success.

• Influence executive leadership through data‑driven sourcing, capability, and risk‑mitigation recommendations.

• Present long‑range strategies, risk models, and capability roadmaps to executive leadership to secure support and resource alignment.

Supply Chain Resilience & Long‑Range Risk Mitigation

• Develop and lead multi‑sourcing strategies, regional supply models, technical capability roadmaps, and Business Continuity Planning (BCP). This includes a strong Single Point of Failure (SPOF) strategy development and execution plan.

• Drive proactive risk identification and escalation processes with Global Supply Chain.

Cross‑Functional Collaboration & Influence

• Collaborate extensively across Product Engineering, NPI, Commodity Management, Operations, Quality, Program Management, and Finance.

• Lead cross‑functional steering teams to synchronize supplier strategies and decision‑making.

• Align global and local supply chain teams to ensure consistent communication and execution.

• Drive organizational alignment and cross‑functional adoption of major initiatives.

Technical Leadership of the Engineering Organization

• Lead and develop a high‑performance engineering team responsible for increasing supplier capability, manufacturability, and technical problem resolution.

• Establish technical standards, methods, and engineering expectations and dissemination into the organization.

Cost Reduction & Value Engineering

•Support a robust cost‑reduction strategy via should‑cost modeling, specification refinement, process optimization and produce re-design via DFM.

• Enable and drive measurable year‑over‑year total landed cost improvements to meet overall BU AOP metrics.

Best Known Methods (BKMs) Development & Dissemination

• Build and scale a comprehensive BKMs portfolio including engineering standards, supplier readiness frameworks, and technical playbooks.

• Drive adoption through structured deployment and global training. Dissemination of learnings is critical to this role.

QUALIFICATIONS

•10 years of experience in Supplier Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain Engineering, Product Development or related fields.

• Strong engineering foundation in semiconductor or high‑reliability systems.

• Proven ability to lead and influence cross‑functional global teams.

• Demonstrated results in supplier development, resilience building, and cost transformation.

• Executive presence, strong communication, and strategic influence capabilities.

• Experience presenting strategy to senior leadership and driving organizational alignment.

The Non-Technical Project Manager is responsible for driving sourcing readiness, supplier selection, and material availability for New Product Introduction (NPI) programs. This role partners closely with the Business Unit and cross-functional engineering teams to manage high‑value consumable and spare parts through the full NPI lifecycle. The ideal candidate brings strong supply chain expertise, experience influencing without authority, and the ability to manage complex part families through sourcing, contracts, and supplier qualification.

Role Responsibilities:

Own sourcing and supplier strategy for high-value consumable and spare parts across NPI programs

Review BOMs and manage part lists and part families, ensuring high‑volume consumables are sourced and dual‑sourced as needed.

Select and qualify suppliers for NPI materials, ensuring capability, capacity, quality, and lead-time alignment.

Review engineering drawings to determine material requirements, manufacturing processes (machining, cleaning, coating), and supplier capability needs.

Ensure contracts, pricing, and lead‑time agreements are established to support program timelines.

Drive supply chain ramp readiness by identifying risks, managing mitigation plans, and ensuring materials are available for build events.

Continue execution of active SRP programs, meeting sourcing metrics such as correct supplier alignment and dual-sourcing requirements.

Engage closely with engineering, BU partners, and supplier focal points to validate part requirements and support testing of critical components.

Lead supplier negotiations and build strong relationships to influence outcomes without direct authority.

Track and report program status, sourcing milestones, supplier readiness, and risks to stakeholders.

Support continuous improvement in sourcing processes, supplier onboarding, and readiness management.

Minimum Qualifications:

4–7 years of experience in supply chain, sourcing, materials management, or related functions.

Supply chain experience required.

Experience managing suppliers, negotiating agreements, and driving sourcing outcomes.

Ability to interpret engineering drawings and understand basic manufacturing processes; technical background helpful but not required.

Strong project management skills with the ability to lead NPI sourcing activities from concept through ramp.

Experience managing through influence and working with cross-functional stakeholders.

Ability to analyze part requirements, supplier capabilities, and risk factors; analytics experience is a plus but not required.

Semiconductor industry experience not required

Role Overview

The Director, SEA Tax is a senior leadership role responsible for overseeing all tax matters across Southeast Asia, while aligning with the global tax strategy.

This role requires a leader who is equally comfortable operating at a strategic level and diving deep into detailed processes, data and technical issues. The successful candidate must be able to understand complex, end‑to‑end tax workflows, identify risks and inefficiencies, and drive sustainable improvements - while also connecting tax outcomes to business strategy, risk management, and operational efficiency.

A critical component of this role is direct people leadership responsibility. Developing a strong, high‑performing team with clear accountability, technical excellence, and continuous improvement mindset is a core expectation of this role.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Regional Tax Leadership & Strategy

Act as the tax leader for SEA, providing oversight across direct tax, indirect tax, withholding tax, transfer pricing, and cross‑border matters.

Translate global tax strategy into strong regional execution that supports business growth while managing tax risk.

Proactively assess emerging tax risks, regulatory developments, and planning opportunities, and advise stakeholders on potential impacts and actions.

2. Tax Compliance, Reporting & Governance

Oversee end‑to‑end tax compliance across SEA, including CIT, GST/VAT, withholding tax, transfer pricing, and incentive‑related reporting.

Ensure timely, accurate quarterly and annual tax accounting deliverables, including tax provision, tax packages, reconciliations, and supporting documentation.

Own SOX tax controls, including design, execution, documentation, and audit readiness.

Maintain strong governance over tax data quality, assumptions, documentation, and controls.

3. Audit, Controversy & Risk Management

Lead all tax audits, assessments, rulings, and appeals across SEA in collaboration with external advisors.

Develop and execute robust audit defense strategies supported by sound technical analysis and documentation.

4. Transfer Pricing & Cross‑Border Matters

Partner with the Global Transfer Pricing team on TP policy, intercompany agreements, documentation and audit support.

Evaluate tax implications of business model changes, supply‑chain restructuring, and new or evolving intercompany arrangements.

Advise on permanent establishment risks, cross‑border services, and intercompany flows.

5. Incentives Governance 

Oversee tax incentive strategy and governance, including applications, compliance with conditions, and ongoing monitoring.

6. Business Partnering & Strategic Projects

Act as a trusted tax advisor to business, finance, legal, and operations leaders.

Provide tax input into strategic initiatives, including M&A, reorganizations, cross‑border structuring, and system implementations.

Ensure tax considerations are embedded early into commercial and operational decision‑making.

7. Process Excellence & Continuous Improvement

Get into the weeds to understand tax processes, systems, and data flows.

Identify inefficiencies, control gaps, and manual workarounds, drive simplification, standardization, and automation where appropriate.

Lead improvements relating to ERP systems, tax reporting tools, and data accuracy.

Embed a mindset of continuous improvement and operational excellence within the tax function.

8. People Leadership

Directly manage and develop the team.

Set clear priorities, performance expectations, and development plans aligned with regional and global objectives.

Provide hands‑on coaching and technical guidance while empowering the team to operate independently.

Build a high‑performing, resilient team with strong succession and retention.

QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Tax, Finance, or related field.

18+ years of progressive tax experience, ideally combining Big 4 and in‑house roles.

Solid tax accounting and SOX/internal controls experience.

Experience in manufacturing, technology, or supply‑chain‑intensive multinational environments.

Prior exposure to tax incentives or large ERP implementations.

Proven leadership experience managing multi‑country tax matters and leading teams.

Demonstrated ability to operate both strategically and hands‑on, with comfort moving between executive discussions and detailed technical work.

CORE COMPETENCIES

Strategic thinker with strong business judgement.

Hands‑on, detail‑oriented, and execution‑focused.

Strong people leader and mentor.

High integrity and accountability.

Comfortable operating in ambiguity and complexity.

As a Process Support Engineer (PSE), you'll play a critical role in guiding products through their entire lifecycle, from initial concept to final qualification. You will provide high-visibility customer support through on-site installations, system diagnoses, and the service and repair of complex systems and equipment. PSEs work closely with customers and R&D teams to develop leading-edge processes used to manufacture advanced semiconductor chips, and create hypothesis experiments and design of experiments (DOEs). You'll analyze data with statistics and compile reports with high-level conclusions on technically challenging process engineering experiments. Additionally, you will troubleshoot complex problems, perform root cause analyses, and resolve difficult process engineering and customer product issues. Process Support Engineers work across technologies such as: Chemical Vapor Deposition, Atomic Layer Deposition, Plasma Reactive Ion Etch, Physical Vapor Deposition, Anneal and Implant.
 

 

Role Responsibilities: 

Provide high-visibility customer support through on-site installations, system diagnoses, and the service and repair of complex systems and equipment 

Work closely with the customer to develop leading-edge processes used to manufacture the most advanced semiconductor chips, many of which are inside everyday electronic devices 

Create hypothesis experiments and design of experiments (DOE); analyze data with statistics; and compile reports with high-level conclusions on technically challenging process engineering experiments 

Troubleshoot complex problems; perform multiple root cause analysis; and resolve a variety of difficult process engineering and customer product issues 

Communicate with both internal stakeholders and the customer to achieve goals with a focus on building relationships and establishing trust 

Apply your growing knowledge of best practices to offer a new perspective using existing solutions 

Serve as a resource for junior colleagues and a liaison between the customer and business unit; you may also lead small projects with manageable risks and resource requirements 

Minimum Qualifications: 

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry/ physics, materials engineering, electrical engineering, optoelectronics or related field 

4–7 years of experience in the semiconductor fab or equipment industry 

Strong interpersonal and communication skills to explain sensitive information and work to build consensus among project stakeholders 

Communication proficiency in English language

Preferred Qualifications: 

Master’s degree or PhD in a related field

PSEs work closely with customers and R&D teams to develop leading-edge processes used to manufacture advanced semiconductor chips, and create hypothesis experiments and design of experiments (DOEs). You'll analyze data with statistics and compile reports with high-level conclusions on technically challenging process engineering experiments. Additionally, you will troubleshoot complex problems, perform root cause analyses, and resolve difficult process engineering and customer product issues. Process Support Engineers work across technologies such as: Chemical Vapor Deposition, Atomic Layer Deposition, Plasma Reactive Ion Etch, Physical Vapor Deposition, Anneal and Implant.
 

 

Role Responsibilities: 

Provide high-visibility customer support through on-site installations, system diagnoses, and the service and repair of complex systems and equipment 

Work closely with the customer to develop leading-edge processes used to manufacture the most advanced semiconductor chips, many of which are inside everyday electronic devices 

Create hypothesis experiments and design of experiments (DOE); analyze data with statistics; and compile reports with high-level conclusions on technically challenging process engineering experiments 

Troubleshoot complex problems; perform multiple root cause analysis; and resolve a variety of difficult process engineering and customer product issues 

Communicate with both internal stakeholders and the customer to achieve goals with a focus on building relationships and establishing trust 

Apply your growing knowledge of best practices to offer a new perspective using existing solutions 

Serve as a resource for junior colleagues and a liaison between the customer and business unit; you may also lead small projects with manageable risks and resource requirements 

Minimum Qualifications: 

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry/ physics, materials engineering, electrical engineering, optoelectronics or related field 

2–5 years of experience in the semiconductor fab or equipment industry 

Strong interpersonal and communication skills to explain sensitive information and work to build consensus among project stakeholders 

Communication proficiency in English language

Preferred Qualifications: 

Master’s degree or PhD in a related field

Update manufacturing instructions

What You'll Be Doing:

Design site layouts for new and existing warehouses using AutoCAD, incorporating operational workflows across inbound, outbound, storage, picking, and shipping.

Select and specify material handling and ancillary equipment, including reach and turret trucks, wire guidance systems, battery/charging systems, racking and shelving specifications, conveyors, AGVs, sorting systems, and dock equipment.

Drive engineering documentation control by creating, maintaining, and governing layouts, specifications, standards, procedures, and work instructions.

Lead end-to-end execution of capital projects, warehouse buildouts, and operational improvement initiatives, from analysis and design through implementation.

Partner with cross-functional teams and vendors to deliver projects on schedule and within budget.

Analyze operational performance and implement practical solutions to improve equipment utilization, workflows, and labor efficiency.

Support and optimize existing automation and material handling systems, troubleshooting issues and implementing enhancements.

Experience working in a distribution center environment.

Experience with material handling equipment and conveyance systems and working with equipment vendors and contractors.

Working knowledge of AutoCAD, Visio, MS Project, Power BI, and basic data analysis tools (VBA/SQL preferred).

Experience developing or supporting engineered labor standards and/or engineering time standards.

Safety-first mindset with the ability to design and implement safe warehouse solutions.

Position:
Due Diligence Analyst

Job Description:

Position Overview:

This position will support the comprehensive due diligence program of Arrow by gathering and analyzing information of new/existing customers and vendors and performing the right level of screening and due diligence based on the potential compliance risks inherent in those external parties. The position acts as a liaison among several internal groups across Arrow global businesses. The position will be based at Shenzhen, China and you will report to the Director Trade Compliance Risk Management EMEA with a dotted line to Senior Compliance Manager in the APAC region.

Our ideal candidate is well-organized, highly analytical with strong attention to detail, multilingual, able to multitask while keeping in line with trade import/export regulations, anti-bribery and anti-corruption (“ABAC”) regulations, anti-money laundering (“AML”) due diligence and deadlines.

What You’ll Be Doing

Screen Arrow’s business partners including customers and vendors using Arrow’s compliance tools and publicly available information.

Analyze information provided by Arrow’s business partners and screening results and determine compliance risks identified for the parties being screened. These risks include but are not limited to:

Fraud risks

Sanction risks

Proliferation risks

Money laundering risks

Bribery and corruption risks

Boycott risks

Follow up with both internal and external stakeholders to ensure the completeness and accurateness of the information provided, and to obtain clarification/justification on potential red flags identified.

Produce accurate & high-quality written summaries and reports to assist with various compliance decision making.

Recommend appropriate measures to mitigate potential compliance risks.

Participate in other compliance activities and ad hoc projects/duties as assigned

What We Are Looking For

Bachelor's degree or above in Finance, Accounting, or Foreign Language Studies

Fresh graduates are welcome; candidates with audit compliance experience and experience working in big organizations are preferred.

Business-fluent English required (interview conducted in English); Fluency in French or Spanish are preferred.

Strong capability in understanding of written and spoken processes, instructions, reports, and regulations.

Strong reading and writing skills, ability to summarize information quickly and effectively from multiple sources into a concise analytical assessment.

Strong cross-functional collaboration skills.

Proficient in MS Office (Word, Excel, Power Point), Oracle experience is a plus.

Self-reliant, and a self-starter with the ability to deal with challenging situations.

Customs process knowledge and trade compliance process understanding are of advantage.

Proven analytical skills

Developed communication and diplomatic skills, verbally and in written form
